name: Simon
overview: Simon, a male disciple of the Messiah, is identified as one of the Twelve apostles chosen by Christ. Known as Simon the Zealot, he is distinguished by his zeal, a unique attribute that sets him apart among the twelve. Scripture records him explicitly as a follower and apostle of YHVH, highlighting his committed role in the early Christian movement.
namesAndTitles: The name Simon means 'he has heard' or 'obedient one,' reflecting a sense of responsiveness or submission. Additionally, he is called Simon the Zealot, indicating his zealous nature. Neither name was given directly by God but both appear in Matthew 10:4, emphasizing his identity and character.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Simon's relationship with YHVH as both disciple and apostle. Beyond these spiritual roles, there is no biblical record of his family or other personal relationships.
scriptureSignificance: Simon the Zealot holds significance as one of the foundational Twelve apostles chosen by Christ to spread the gospel. His designation as 'the zealot' suggests a fervent dedication to the Messiah's mission. His inclusion in Matthew 10:2 and 10:4 affirms his integral role in the early church and the establishment of Christ's followers.
